message: Good point about the location from which cadets might feel or inhabit perspectives. There is, though, a sense of community here that feels much more tight than anywhere else I've taught, coming partly from the fraction of cadets who are prior service, partly from the strong family service traditions, partly from the whole immersion thing that goes on here, and partly from just the way the military is: in terms of camaraderie, my time in the military was the best job I've every had. While what I'm doing now is far more intellectually fulfilling, I won't forget the sense of shared commitment that was so immensely and uniquely rewarding when I was a soldier. And yet that tension between intellectual fulfillment and shared commitment that Joanna brings up is something that sometimes confounds and frustrates me here: cadets are soldiers first, and I know and respect that, but that means that they're not intellectuals, scholars, or students first -- and that frequently comes out in the attitudes about the place of academics.
